title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §1.11 of the expanded typescript of the May 1966 letter to Tate on crystals. On the previous page Grothendieck localised the Z_p-linear abelian category of crystals of modules on S at p: the objects stay the same and each Hom is replaced by Hom⊗Q. The result is 'crystals up to isogeny', i.e. isocrystals.

(1) A p-isocrystal is an isocrystal M with a morphism F: M^(p) → M, where M^(p) is the Frobenius pull-back. In modern terms this is an F-isocrystal, with F not yet assumed invertible.

(2) Grothendieck observes that the weight-i notion copied from bicrystals (F, V with FV = p^i, VF = p^i) is redundant up to isogeny. Once p is invertible, V is forced to equal p^i F^{-1}. So he defines a bi-isocrystal as a p-isocrystal whose F is an isomorphism. This is the modern notion of a (non-degenerate) F-isocrystal. He deliberately does not fix a weight, and he drops 'p^{-1}-isocrystals' as superfluous.

(3) Duality: for objects of finite type the category is self-dual. The dual of (M, F) is (M^∨, ᵗF^{-1}), using (M^∨)^(p) = (M^(p))^∨.

(4) Localising the category Bicr(S,i) of weight-i bicrystals at p gives an abelian category Isbicr(S,i). The exact 'forget V' functor Isbicr(S,i) → Isbicr(S) is fully faithful, because V = p^i F^{-1} is determined by F.

(5) There are transition functors Bicr(S,i) → Bicr(S,i+1), (M,F,V) ↦ (M,F,pV). After inverting p these become fully faithful. So 'bicrystals of weight i up to isogeny', for increasing i, give ever larger generalisations of Dieudonné crystals (weight 1). All of them embed in the bi-isocrystals. The next page adds that this category is stable under ⊗ and duals, and proposes it as the natural target category for an isogeny-level de Rham cohomology functor.

Over a perfect field (next page) a bi-isocrystal is a finite-dimensional K = Frac W(k) vector space with a bijective σ-semilinear endomorphism. The essential image of weight i corresponds to isocrystals admitting an F-stable lattice M with p^i M ⊂ F(M) ⊂ M, i.e. slopes in [0,i]. Grothendieck does not state this slope description here.

The problem served is to find the right coefficient or value category for crystalline (de Rham) cohomology of higher degree in characteristic p, extending Dieudonné theory, which handles degree 1 and p-divisible groups.
errors: No mathematical errors. The full-faithfulness claims are correct and essentially formal, since V is determined by F once p is inverted.

The claim that Isbicr(S,i) is abelian is fine, as the localisation of an abelian category at a Serre subcategory, provided Bicr(S,i) is abelian. Grothendieck does not justify the latter for general S here.
Typo 'isogristaux' for 'isocristaux' in the first line (typescript error).

ideas.what: Isocrystals as crystals of modules up to isogeny (Hom⊗Q), and p-isocrystals with F: M^(p) → M
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966 letter to Tate, IHES lectures 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes'); developed by Berthelot and Ogus
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968); letter to Tate 1966 (circulated)

ideas.what: Bi-isocrystal = F-isocrystal with F an isomorphism, weight-free, replacing (F,V) pairs; V = p^i F^{-1} redundant
Bicrystals of weight i (FV = VF = p^i), transition functors (M,F,V) ↦ (M,F,pV), fully faithful embeddings up to isogeny into F-isocrystals
ideas.modern_name: F-crystals with slopes in [0,i] / Dieudonné-type crystals of level i (Mazur, Ogus 'F-crystals of level i')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck 1966 for the idea; Mazur (Frobenius and the Hodge filtration), Berthelot–Ogus for systematic use

ideas.what: F-isocrystals as the natural value category of de Rham/crystalline cohomology up to isogeny
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known 1966 Tate-letter material introducing isocrystals and F-isocrystals. The constructions are formal and have long since become standard, credited to Grothendieck. Nothing on the page is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: First line: the typescript reads 'isogristaux' (typo for 'isocristaux').
The abelian category is 'Isbicr(S,i)' (typed 'Iscr' with 'bi' inserted by hand). The transcription 'Is[-cr-]{+bi+}r(S,i)' garbles this.
In the displayed forgetful functor, the typescript has 'Isbicr(S),i)' corrected to 'Isbicr(S,i) → Isbicr(S)'.
The exponent in 'p^{i}F^{-1}' carries a handwritten mark (looks like ± or *) before i; the reading p^i F^{-1} is mathematically correct.
'Quand on localise ces foncteurs par p': 'par' is handwritten over a typed word.
The struck-out passage reads approximately: 'si Ø est un foncteur contravariant de catégories fibrées sur en...'.
